The corpus's cut is the one the onset vocabulary supports, and the collision pattern named for that pair does not hold there: MT 28:24 carries neither a behold-I-am-against clause nor a messenger formula, unlike the companion cases at MT 26:6->26:7 and MT 29:9->29:10. Two rows of this cluster stand on that reading; reconciling plan and corpus is above one lens.
The same plan lists Ezek.26.15-26.21 under both the nation-oracle type and the lament type. The row chose the former with a byte reason; the ambiguity is in the source list, not the row.

The one class deserving a ruling is the verse on the far side of a row's own seam, which the both-sides law makes that row's own evidence while the convention keeps it in prose. Corpus-wide convention question; I filed none as a per-row defect.
